title: Witten: Townsend Brown's antigravity bismuth isotope

tellings.quote: he says that he was contracted by right Airfield to work on gravity and he said that there was a guy named townzen who had a weird isotope of bismuth that exhibited anti-gravity properties

plain: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays what a physicist named Louis Witten said about the 1950s. According to Michels, Witten said he was hired through Wright Field, a US Air Force base, to work on gravity, with a link to the Martin Corporation, an aircraft maker. Witten also said a man named T. Townsend Brown had an unusual form of the metal bismuth that seemed to resist gravity, which would mean antigravity research was quietly under way back then.
